interpretation.interpretation: The diagram appears to show a human head in profile at the centre of a circle (a microcosm figure) from which twelve rays extend to twelve interlace-decorated triangles on the rim. This arrangement is most likely a schematic of the twelve winds, or twelve directional points, arranged around the circle of the world or of the cosmos, with the human head at the centre. The colours alternate in a pattern, yellow at the four cardinal positions (top, bottom, left, right) and blue at the other eight. This suggests a distinction between principal and secondary winds or directions. The cropped text above the circle, in which only "flante" is legible, would fit a nearby passage on blowing or breath (spiritus/flatus), which supports a wind reading. The link between the central head and the winds could express the idea of the human being as a microcosm that corresponds to the structure of the cosmos. The text is too fragmentary to confirm this reading.
interpretation.evidence: The layout is a central circle with twelve radiating lines ending in triangles on the outer circle, which is a common wind-rose or twelve-part scheme. The four yellow triangles sit at the cardinal points and the eight blue triangles sit between them. Step 1 recorded only a fragmentary, partly illegible text ("flante") that is cropped and not part of the diagram proper, so the textual support is weak. The diagram carries no labels naming the winds, directions or head, so the identification of the triangles as winds, and of the head as a microcosm or a specific figure, rests on a general diagrammatic tradition and is not confirmed by the diagram itself. Step 1 also did not record the exact position of the text relative to the circle, and its "above" relation to the outer circle is uncertain. The 'twelve' count and the cardinal/intercardinal colour pattern are visible in Step 1 entries.
